thread:
jia: Quick Q — where's the canonical PagerDuty playbook that maps alerts to escalation paths? Need to reference it for the alert-pruning RFC. Also our repo-deploy alert fires 4x per deploy, thinking of proposing a filter.

sam: It's in the runbook repo: https://git.internal/runbooks/pagerduty-escalations — but some teams keep local overrides. Which alert are you looking at?

jia: infra.repo-deploy.failure (openshift). It's noisy during batch CI jobs.

alex: For that alert we added a suppression window last year. See dashboard link: https://dashboards.redwood/alerts/infra-repo-deploy. It has a PD service mapping to infra-oncall -> infra-lead.

maria: If you're proposing a filter, consider matching `ci_job_type != "batch"` instead of global rate-limiting; easier to reason about. Example rule:

```
filter:
  - alert: infra.repo-deploy.failure
    expression: ci_job_type != "batch"
```

That would stop the CI fanout without hiding real deploy failures.

sam: Also check PD integration mapping in ops/config/pd-routing.yaml — if you change tags, make sure mapping still matches (service_key/tag selectors).

jia: Thanks. Can someone paste the PD escalation link for infra-oncall? I need to add it to the RFC.

oncall-bot: Incident response playbooks: https://pagerduty.com/playbooks/infra-oncall. Last updated 2025-11-19 by alex.

alex: ^ correct. Also ping @devops-jen to confirm she is ok with the filter. @devops-jen?

devops-jen: I'm fine with filtering by ci_job_type, but let's make it a canary for a week (add `suppression_duration: 7d` flagged on rollout). Also add a metric in the dashboard to track suppressed alerts (count of suppressed firing alerts).

maria: I'll open a PR with the YAML and dashboard change, link it here when ready.

jia: Perfect — please tag me on the PR. Thanks all :thumbsup:
